package_info.why_malicious: This report does not describe a specific malicious package, but rather analyzes several high-profile CI/CD supply chain breaches and the associated risks. The macro-level reasoning is that these incidents involved unauthorized code changes, credential leaks, and artifact tampering, all of which enabled attackers to compromise software supply chains and exfiltrate sensitive data.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious code injected into PHP source repository (exact code not shown in report)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At commit-time, the attacker injects malicious code into the PHP repository, which is then distributed to downstream users via official channels, enabling remote code execution or backdoor access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unauthorized code changes to a core repository are highly suspicious, especially when they introduce new, undocumented functionality.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal commits to core repositories are reviewed and validated; malicious commits bypass these controls.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate code changes by authorized maintainers.
key_indicators: Unexpected code changes in core repositories
Lack of proper code review or validation
Distribution of modified artifacts to users

execution_context.file_location: CI build scripts (Codecov Bash uploader script)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Modified Bash uploader script exfiltrates environment variables to attacker-controlled server (exact code not shown in report)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During CI pipeline execution, the modified script reads environment variables (including secrets) and sends them to an external server, resulting in credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: CI scripts should not exfiltrate secrets to unknown domains.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal CI scripts upload coverage data to trusted endpoints, not arbitrary external servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Uploading coverage data to official Codecov servers.
key_indicators: Network requests to untrusted domains during CI

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Pipeline exposes secrets (API keys, tokens) to build logs or external parties (exact code not shown in report)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During pipeline execution, secrets stored in environment variables are inadvertently exposed to build logs or accessible by unauthorized parties, leading to credential leakage.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Secrets should never be exposed in logs or to unauthorized users.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Build environments are expected to protect secrets and restrict access.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; secrets should always be protected.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious package published to public registry with same name as internal dependency (dependency confusion, exact code not shown in report)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During dependency resolution, the build system installs a malicious package from a public registry instead of the intended internal package, allowing attacker code to execute in the build environment.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unexpected packages from public registries should not be installed in place of internal dependencies.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Dependency resolution should prioritize trusted, internal sources.
key_indicators: Unexpected package source in dependency resolution
Execution of unreviewed code during build

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains unauthorized access to code repository or CI/CD environment.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code or configuration is introduced into the pipeline.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code or configuration is executed during build or deployment.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive data (secrets, credentials) is accessed or exfiltrated.

attack_chain.action: Compromised artifacts or secrets are distributed to downstream users or attackers.
attack_chain.leads_to: Widespread compromise of user environments or further lateral movement.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected code changes in core repositories
CI/CD scripts making network requests to untrusted domains
Secrets or environment variables accessed or exfiltrated during builds
Installation of dependencies from unexpected sources
file_indicators: Modified build scripts (e.g., Bash uploader, YAML workflows)
Unexpected changes in package.json or requirements.txt
network_indicators: Outbound requests to unknown or attacker-controlled domains during CI/CD execution
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unauthorized changes to core repositories and build scripts, alert on CI/CD pipeline network activity to untrusted domains, scan build logs for exposed secrets, and validate the source of all dependencies during builds. Implement artifact integrity validation and enforce strict access controls on CI/CD environments.
